annotations.title: Link a segment to a campaign

description: Make a segment one of the campaign's audiences. The contacts it matches now become leads, and, on a sequence campaign that is running, so does everyone who joins it later (checked every 2 minutes). A one-time campaign takes the members it has when it launches, and no more. `revision` is the segment's revision you read: it is your approval of exactly that audience, and if the segment changed since, nothing is linked and it answers 409. Link it again at the new revision to approve it again. Each lead goes through the same checks as add_campaign_leads (suppression, the list gate, the key's limits), and on a running campaign the same permission and approval: `operate` while it is a draft, `send` once it holds an approval, and the caller becomes its approver. A contact you removed by hand stays out. A campaign links up to 10 segments. A segment edit never changes what a running campaign sends: it holds that link's new leads until someone approves it again. On a running campaign, a change that adds to what it sends or to whom also needs the `send` permission, and makes the caller its approver. Through an API key an owner limited, the key's limits must cover the campaign, every mailbox it sends from and outreach, or it answers 403 with `details.scope` naming the limit. A change that only takes something out needs none of that.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

revision.description: The segment's revision you read. It is your approval: the campaign takes in contacts that match that version of the segment. If the segment changed since, nothing is linked and it answers 409 `segmentStale`; read it again, then link at the new revision. Linking a segment that is already linked, at its newer revision, approves it again.

segmentId.description: The segment to link: its id from list_segments.
